I. $(11,10)$

current_example.problem:
Which of the following pairs $(x,y)$ are solutions of the Diophantine equation $3x+8y=5?$

I. $(7,-2)$

II. $(22,-8)$

III. $(15,-5)$
current_example.worked_solution:
Let's check each pair in turn.

- $(7,-2)$ is a solution of our equation. Indeed, substituting $x=7$ and $y=-2,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+8y & =5 \\ 3\cdot 7+8\cdot (-2) & =5 \\ 21-16 & =5 \\ 5 & =5\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- $(22,-8)$ is *not* a solution of our equation. Substituting $x=22$ and $y=-8,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+8y & =5 \\ 3\cdot 22+8\cdot (-8) & =5 \\ 66-64 & =5 \\ 2 & \ne 5\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

- $(15,-5)$ is a solution of our equation. Indeed, substituting $x=15$ and $y=-5,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+8y & =5 \\ 3\cdot 15+8\cdot (-5) & =5 \\ 45-40 & =5 \\ 5 & =5\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
